sarah (support): FYI — customer 'BrightMetrics' opened a support -> sales request asking for: Terraform provider to provision dedicated deployments, Python SDK convenience helpers for streaming, and SSO/SCIM provisioning. They flagged compliance needs. Ticket: BM-4123.
elaine (product): thx Sarah. Can you paste the customer ask text or paste the sales convo? need clarifying Qs: 1) Terraform - is it for provisioning infra or mapping to our 'dedicated' product config? 2) SCIM: full provisioning vs just SCIM SSO mapping? 3) Python SDK: is this small helper or a maintained package?
raj (sales): copied excerpt from the convo: "we need our infra-as-code to wire up dedicated capacity, enroll service-accounts, and set RBAC automatically. Also SAML+SCIM to push users from Okta. Our infra team prefers Terraform." They said devs want a nicer Python streaming client that handles reconnect + token refresh. ARR potential: ~$60k ARR first year if we deliver in Q3.
danny (devex): tagging maintenance concerns — if we publish an official python package we should commit to semver + monthly releases for security patches. Might be easier to publish community examples first.
matt (eng): rough engineering take: Terraform provider for provisioning dedicated capacity = ~5-8w (initial MVP) assuming we reuse the existing control-plane APIs. SCIM full provisioning + provisioning lifecycle (deprovision, group sync) = ~3-6w. Python SDK helper for streaming + token refresh = ~2w. But that's parallelizable to some extent.
elaine (product): ok here's my proposal for intake -> triage: 1) Split into 3 tickets: infra-provider (terraform), scim/provisioning, python-sdk-streaming. 2) For each ticket set: minimal launch criteria, owner, and tag metadata (priority, cust, team). 3) Decide initial priority based on revenue impact + security/regulatory needs. 4) If terraform + scim must ship together for this customer, mark as unblocker.
sarah (support): customer says they need provisioning + SCIM together to start migrating in 8 weeks. They can accept a staged rollout for python SDK.
elaine (product): proposed tags and fields (please confirm): - priority: P1 (if sales confirms migration start) or P2 otherwise - integration-type: terraform, scim, sdk-python - customer: brightmetrics - launch-criteria: docs + terraform examples + e2e (dedicated provisioning) for terraform; SCIM must support create/update/deactivate + audit logs + sample Okta config; Python SDK must have streaming example, token refresh helper, and published package on PyPI + publish notes. - owner: eng-platform for terraform, eng-ml for python helper? open to suggestions.
raj (sales): confirm we need P1. They said migration starts in ~8 weeks, onboarding window is tight. I can push to contract to include a co-delivery milestone.
danny (devex): agree on sample-first approach: for python, publish a small reference repo + example usage in docs, then package later. reduces maintenance burden. Also recommend a 'community-preview' tag and deprecation warnings if API changes.
matt (eng): engineering owners: eng-platform should lead terraform + control-plane APIs, eng-ml can pair on python streaming helper. SCIM probably sits with eng-platform + security for audit. Need to scope an MVP for each: Terraform MVP = create/destroy dedicated + set named config + attach billing profile; SCIM MVP = user create/update/deactivate + group membership basic sync + OAuth2 bearer for token exchange; Python SDK MVP = streaming client wrapper + token refresh helper + simple readme.
elaine (product): good. I'll create the intake tickets and tag them per the schema we use. Proposed backlog tags (exact values): ["priority:P1","integration:terraform","integration:scim","sdk:python","customer:brightmetrics","revenue:60k","compliance:high","release-window:Q3"]
sarah (support): please include acceptance criteria that support can validate during onboarding (e.g., run terraform sample, SCIM changes show up within 30s, streaming reconnects within 2s).
request-bot: Created ticket RF-2317 (terraform-provider) assigned to eng-platform. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RF-2317
request-bot: Created ticket RF-2318 (scim-provisioning) assigned to eng-platform + security. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RF-2318
request-bot: Created ticket RF-2319 (python-stream-helper) assigned to eng-ml + devex. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RF-2319
elaine (product): next steps: - Raj to confirm contract milestone and hard go-live date by EOD Fri - Matt to add initial estimates + list of API gaps by Tue - Danny to draft devex plan for publishing + maintenance notes - Sarah to add onboarding acceptance tests to RF tickets
raj (sales): I’ll confirm dates. quick ask: add tag "enterprise:onprem" — customer is evaluating VPC/private deployment.
elaine (product): added tag suggestion. Final question: does anyone object to shipping terraform+scim as a bundled P1?
danny (devex): no objection given customer need, but recommend we gate GA on docs + sample terraform module + SCIM Okta sample.
matt (eng): agree. If scope creeps we should split incremental rollouts: MVP -> beta -> GA.
elaine (product): perfect. I'll update the RF tickets with these launch criteria + tags. Thanks all :thumbsup:
